result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both use a diverging bar chart with plan as the zero line, sort shops from furthest ahead to furthest behind, label Northfield 'on plan', and keep blue/orange or red only for ahead/behind, so they score almost the same. A labels each shop right beside its bar, shows the gap in both % and $K, and uses a light page that is safer in email clients; B's dark card background is risky in many mail clients and its shop names sit far from the bars. B's actual-vs-plan column is a nice touch, but it doesn't make up for that. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both are well-sorted diverging bar charts of percentage gap from plan, and both label Northfield as on plan. B has a bold plan baseline, right-aligned shop names close to their bars, blue/orange colors that colour-blind readers can tell apart, and a light background that suits email. A's faint zero line and left-aligned names far from the bars make the reference weaker, and its dark card may render poorly in email clients, though its actual-vs-plan column is a nice touch.
